newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican says it won't extend ADE debt-relief plan.
newsitem.headline: Mexican says it won't extend ADE debt-relief plan.

text.p: Mexico will not extend the application deadline for the ADE debt-relief program beyond September 30, Finance Ministry spokesman Alejandro Valenzuela said on Wednesday.

The Support for Bank Debtors (ADE) is a wide-ranging plan launched by the Mexican government to help debtors pay back loans to banks after interest rates soared following the December 1994 peso devaluation.
"With regard to the ADE, there will not be an extension," Valenzuela told a news conference. "This will end on September 30 as it was originally agreed."
The ADE deadline has been extended at least twice, first from January 31 until April 30 and then from April 30 until September 31.
However, the second extension only pertained to restructuring debt in UDI bonds.
Valenuzela stressed that debtors must act quickly if they want to apply for relief under the plan.
